habitat: Singly in large trees in bushveld and open savanna, especially along rivers and watercourses.
summary: A fairly common resident. A large, uniformly grey owl, paler below, with a black outline to the facial disc, dark eyes and pink eyelids. The immature is browner. The underparts are finely barred. The voice is a series of deep grunts, and the female and young give a long whistle. The page uses Bubo lacteus. This list keeps Ketupa lactea. The Kemp name Giant Eagle Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: The large northern race of Cape Eagle-Owl has blotchy underparts. Verreaux's Eagle-Owl has dark eyes and finely barred underparts.
Pel's Fishing Owl can be confused with it in a quick view in a tall riverine tree. Pel's has cinnamon underparts and rufous-brown upperparts.

head.pattern: Facial disc with a black outline. The eyes are dark and the eyelids are pink. Ear tufts are not always raised.

upperparts.pattern: Uniformly grey. The immature is browner.

underparts.pattern: Paler grey below and finely barred, not blotchy.

head.pattern: Immature is browner. The eyes are dark.

calls.description: A series of deep grunts, 'hu-hu-hu, hu-hu'. The female and young utter a long drawn-out whistle. The grade A call is from Kruger, near Sabie Park. The catalogue still files the species as Bubo lacteus. The filename is XC1007496-20240222_KNP_NSerpa_XA60_A001C113_240222HO_CANON_SLE_-3dBNORM.wav.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The eyes are only described as dark, so no iris colour is stored. The page uses Bubo lacteus, and the recording catalogue does too. The grade A call is from Kruger. The Kemp name Giant Eagle Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^9=512 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 256–1024.
